content.title: ‘No Kings’ protests return Saturday across Southwest and Central Virginia
content.text: ROANOKE, Va. (WDBJ) - Cities across the country are rolling out the stage equipment and barricades as they prepare for crowds this weekend for the No Kings rally.More than 3,000 rallies are scheduled across all 50 states, a nationwide show of people planning to take their message to the streets Saturday, March 28, for the third time . The “No Kings” movement began last summer as a coordinated protest against President Donald Trump’s administration and policies. “Here is your opportunity to come out and show that we as people are standing together and want to be heard,” said Roanoke Indivisible organizer Rachel Gray. In October, at least 7 million protesters joined demonstrations. That same month, President Trump spoke out against the “No Kings” title. “I’m no king, I work hard to make this country great, that’s all it is. I’m not a king at all,” said Trump. According to CBS News, Saturday’s rally is expected to be the largest yet for many cities. Gray said recent national and international conflicts could be the reason for the growing numbers.“The war that’s happening currently and this crazy secret police force in our street is doing stuff that’s concerning to everybody. It gives us all an opportunity to go, ' I don’t agree with the way the system is working right now, and this is what I think we should do,” said Gray. In St. Paul, Minnesota, law enforcement is preparing for large crowds.“We have numbers ranging from 50,000 to 150,000,” said St. Paul Police Senior Commander Jesse Mollner.And in downtown Los Angeles, officials have installed metal gates at some street on- and offramps ahead of Saturday’s protests. They say it’s a proactive step—meant to keep demonstrators from entering the freeway if crowds grow near City Hall.Roanoke’s “No Kings” rally will be held from noon to 2 p.m. at Elmwood Park.“Things are really scary right now, and everybody is unsure of so much. So being able to connect with somebody to say, ‘Hey, I feel the same way you do,’ or ‘everything is just kind of a lot’—is a good way to feel better together," said Gray. Other local rallies:Blacksburg: 3 to 6 p.m. on Henderson Lawn (at Main St. and College Ave in Blacksburg)Lynchburg: 10 a.m. -1 p.m. at Miller ParkRocky Mount: 11 a.m. - 2 p.m., location not listedCovington: 10 a.m. - noon at South Craig Avenue & South Lexington AvenueWDBJ reached out to local Republican groups in response to these upcoming protests. Roanoke County Republican Committee Chairman Michael Walsh said:“I’m glad to hear of the No Kings protest tomorrow against the self-coronation of politicians in Richmond who are pushing one of the worst congressional gerrymanders in the nation. Those same politicians in the House of Delegates and State Senate spent weeks of the General Assembly Session fighting over who would run for Congress and how they could best carve up our communities to their advantage. They campaigned on affordability, but instead made a power grab for their own personal gain, the number one priority.”Copyright 2026 WDBJ. All rights reserved.
